_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::scalar_transport#5 — BDF2 needs no hand-written start-up because 4C already takes one backward-Euler step, shown by an exact equality rather than an error table. The same deck under TIMEINTEGR 'BDF2' and under 'One_Step_Theta' with THETA 1.0: after ONE step the two agree to the last printed digit (-1.09579033878309936e-03 both), after two and after four steps they differ (2.06429074665608718e-02 vs 2.48230383072740556e-02). The later-step disagreement is what stops the first result being vacuous — if BDF2 never engaged, every step would agree. 4C announces none of this (STARTUP_ANNOUNCED=0); the switch is visible only in the numbers. Confirmed in source at src/scatra/4C_scatra_timint_bdf2.cpp, where set_old_part_of_righthandside uses theta=1.0 for step 1 and 2/3 thereafter. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: run the 'BDF2' arm as One_Step_Theta as well. Every step then agrees, LATER_STEPS_DIFFER flips to no, and the fixture must go red — that assertion is what proves BDF2 really engages after step 1.
break the comparison the other way: make the control something that is NOT backward Euler by giving the One_Step_Theta arm a different scheme. The one-step equality fails and the fixture must go red.
